card_desc: One task a day for 30 days. Set up your CRM, automate the work you repeat, then bring in AI.
meta_title: The 30-Day CRM & AI Build Checklist (Free) | Olivia Porter
meta_description: A free 30-day checklist for B2B owners with a small team: set up your CRM so it tells the truth, automate the work you repeat, then bring in AI. One task a day.
sub: For B2B owners with a small team. One task a day: set up your CRM, automate the work you repeat, then bring in AI.
intro: You started your business for freedom. This is how you start getting your time back: set up your CRM so it tells the truth, automate the work you repeat, then bring in AI. In that order.
AI can't fix a messy system. It just repeats the mess faster.

before.label: Two things before you start
items: Most owners skip week 1. Please don't. You can only get your time back if you know where it's going.
Check off each day as you go.
Your progress saves in this browser, so you can come back tomorrow and pick up where you left off.

steps.title: Start a time log
steps.text: Write down where every 15 minutes of your day goes. A spreadsheet or a notebook is fine. Keep it going all week.

steps.title: List what depends on you
steps.text: Write down everything that waits on you: approvals, sales decisions, customer questions, admin work.

steps.title: Pick one source of truth
steps.text: Decide which system holds your customers, deals, and follow-ups. That's your CRM. Not your inbox, not a spreadsheet.

steps.title: Write your CRM's three jobs
steps.text: Write down the three things your CRM actually needs to do. For example: track leads, manage follow-ups, and show which deals are about to close. Start there.

steps.title: Get the structure right
steps.text: A contact is a person. A company is where they work. A deal is money in motion, with a stage, an amount, and a close date. Don't put deal info on the contact.

steps.title: Make four fields required
steps.text: On new records, require name and best contact, lead source, stage, and owner. Only add a new field when you'll filter or report on it.

steps.title: Review your time log
steps.text: Circle the task you repeat the most. Sort the rest into three lists: only you can do it, your team could do it, a tool could do it.

sections.label: Week 2 · Days 8 to 14
sections.title: Make your CRM tell the truth

steps.title: Name stages after buyer actions
steps.text: Name each pipeline stage after something the buyer did. "Interested" is a feeling. "Demo booked" is a fact. Write the rule for moving from one stage to the next. A simple start: New lead, Qualified, Proposal sent, Negotiation, Closed.

steps.title: Give every deal a next step
steps.text: Filter your open deals with no next step. Give each one a step and a date. Close the ones you can't.

steps.title: Turn report fields into dropdowns
steps.text: Make the fields you report on into dropdowns: lead source, industry, company size, lost reason. Keep one notes field for everything else. Notes are for the story. Fields are for the facts.

steps.title: Make every follow-up a task
steps.text: Every follow-up becomes a task in your CRM with a due date. Check one task list every morning.

steps.title: Connect your email
steps.text: Connect your email to your CRM, or at least log the important conversations there. If it matters to revenue, it lives in the CRM.

steps.title: Save your top email templates
steps.text: Find the emails you type every week. Write your best version once and save it as a CRM template with merge fields for first name and company.

steps.title: Ask your team what they need
steps.text: Ask the people who use the CRM every day what would make their job easier. Hide the fields nobody uses. Build what they ask for first.

steps.title: List your copy-paste work
steps.text: Look at everything your team copies and pastes from one tool to another. List each one. Those systems should be connected.

steps.title: Build your first automation
steps.text: Build the one automation that saves you the most time. Pick from these five:
list: Capture new leads in your CRM automatically
Create a follow-up task when a new inquiry comes in
Create the project and onboarding checklist when a deal closes
Automate recurring invoices and payment reminders
Send yourself a daily summary of important business activity

steps.title: Test it with real records
steps.text: Run it on real records. Fix what breaks before you add anything else.

steps.title: Build the next one
steps.text: Build the next automation on your list.

steps.title: Test that one too
steps.text: Test it the same way. One at a time, every time.

steps.title: Sort automation vs. AI
steps.text: Sort what's left. Use regular automation when data just needs to move from one place to another. Save AI for when information needs to be summarized, sorted, or interpreted.

steps.title: Count the hours you got back
steps.text: Write down the hours you got back this week. Compare it to your week 1 time log.

steps.title: Pick one AI tool
steps.text: Pick one AI tool and stick with it for a month. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, whichever you already use.

steps.title: Write your never-paste list
steps.text: Passwords and logins. Bank, card, and tax ID numbers. Client data you're not authorized to share. Employee HR details. If you wouldn't put it on a billboard, don't put it in your chat.

steps.title: Teach it your business
steps.text: Tell it about your business before you ask it anything. Give it six things:
list: What you sell and what it costs
The questions customers always ask, with your answers
What you never want it to say

steps.title: Save three weekly prompts
steps.text: Write prompts for three tasks you do every week and save them. Add this line to each one: "Ask me questions before you answer."

steps.title: Connect AI to your tools
steps.text: Connect your AI to your email, calendar, and CRM. Only share customer data with a tool your company has approved for it. Otherwise strip out names and sensitive info first.

steps.title: Hand it one real task
steps.text: Paste in messy call notes and use the prompt below. Check the work before you put it in your CRM.
steps.prompt:
Here are my notes from a sales call. Give me:
1. A 3-line summary
2. The customer's main problem
3. The next step, with a date
4. Any risks to the deal

Ask me questions before you answer.

[paste your notes here]

steps.title: Triage your inbox
steps.text: Sort your inbox into three groups: needs a decision from you, can be delegated, can be handled by an automation. Let AI summarize and draft replies, with the right privacy controls.

sections.label: Days 29 and 30
sections.title: Protect the time you got back

steps.title: Build one morning dashboard
steps.text: Build one dashboard you check every morning:

steps.title: Block the time you got back
steps.text: Put the hours you got back on your calendar. More time doesn't mean more work. Then ask: if I stepped away for 7 days, would leads still get followed up and deals still move forward? Whatever stops is next month's list.

closing: That's 30 days. If you did them in order, your CRM tells the truth, the repeat work runs itself, and AI is working from real data instead of guesses.
